sourceAgencies: NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits (SHBP / SEHBP)
City of Clifton 2026 Adopted Municipal Budget (Sheet 3b(2) & Sheet 19)
Clifton Board of Education User-Friendly Budget
NJ Office of the State Comptroller (OSC)

overview.percentageOfCombinedBudgets: 23.7% of all Clifton municipal and school spending ($103.4M of $436.5M) goes directly to employee health insurance, pensions, and retirement benefits

healthcarePlans.providers: State Health Benefits Program (SHBP) for Municipal & School Employees' Health Benefits Program (SEHBP) for Board of Ed

primaryPlans.planName: NJ DIRECT 10 / NJ DIRECT 15 (Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield)
primaryPlans.description: Comprehensive statewide and nationwide network with $10 or $15 primary care copays, low in-network deductibles ($100-$400), and 100% preventive care coverage.

Created under P.L. 2020, c. 44 for teachers and school staff. Caps employee contribution to a percentage of base salary (1.7% - 7.2%) rather than a percentage of insurance premium, shifting more cost to the school district.
Lower out-of-pocket costs at Tier 1 designated hospitals and physicians (e.g. St. Joseph's Health, Hackensack Meridian).
Carve-out prescription coverage. Low copays ($3 generic, $10 preferred brand, $25 non-preferred). Taxpayer covers remaining cost of specialty drugs.
Full preventive and restorative dental coverage (up to $1,500 - $2,000 annual maximum per member) and biennial optical exams/glasses allowances.

rules.employeeContribution: 3.0% to 35.0% of insurance premium based on salary tier
rules.note: For an employee earning $120,000 with family coverage costing $34,000/year, the employee pays ~35% ($11,900) while the City of Clifton taxpayer pays 65% ($22,100/year).
A teacher making $75,000 pays ~4.5% of salary ($3,375), while the Board of Education pays the remaining ~$28,000+ family premium cost.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Multi-million dollar unfunded other post-employment benefits (OPEB) liability
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: City employees and teachers who retire with 25 or more years of credited service in the state pension system receive 100% employer-provided health insurance coverage for themselves and eligible dependents until eligible for Medicare, plus Medicare Part B reimbursement.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.legalAuthority: NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits (N.J.S.A. 43:16A & 43:15A)
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: City pays $14.85M annually into PFRS ($12.11M) and PERS ($2.74M)
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Mandatory employer pension billings certified by the NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits: $12,111,760 for Clifton Police & Firemen's Retirement System (PFRS) and $2,742,598 for Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS). School educators participate in TPAF (funded via State direct appropriation).

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.benefitName: Accumulated Sick Leave & Terminal Leave Payouts
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Significant lump-sum liability upon employee retirements
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Under New Jersey P.L. 2010, c. 3, sick leave payouts for employees hired after May 21, 2010 are supposed to be capped at $15,000. However, the NJ State Comptroller found that five of Clifton's union contracts bypassed or omitted this cap, permitting employees to accumulate and cash out up to 260 unused sick days upon departure.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Direct cash payments of $450,000 budgeted in 2026
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Official 2026 Adopted Budget Sheet 3b(2) documents 116 municipal employees electing health benefits waiver opt-out cash stipends totaling $450,000 annually under N.J.S.A. 40A:10-17.1.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.legalAuthority: PBA Local 36, FMBA Local 21, and DPW Union Guides
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Automatic 2% to 10%+ base salary step increases
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Police officers, firefighters, and senior DPW staff receive automatic longevity step percentage increases added directly to base pay after 5, 10, 15, and 20 years of municipal service.
